root_cause.text: The x86 CR4 pinning code incorrectly included `X86_CR4_FRED` in `cr4_pinned_mask`, which forced FRED to stay enabled during boot even though FRED MSRs are not yet initialized on all CPUs, creating a window where exceptions cannot be handled and guests can triple fault.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `X86_CR4_FRED` from `cr4_pinned_mask` in `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/common.c`, and the CVE description states that “when during boot FRED is initialized: first on the BSP and later on the APs” there is “a window in time when exceptions cannot be handled,” especially causing SEV/TDX guests to “triple fault due to FRED MSRs not being set up yet.”

vuln_statements.content: static const unsigned long cr4_pinned_mask = X86_CR4_SMEP | X86_CR4_SMAP | X86_CR4_UMIP |

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove FRED from the CR4 pinned mask so CR4 pinning does not incorrectly lock that bit after CPU initialization.
intent_record.what: The `cr4_pinned_mask` constant was changed by removing `X86_CR4_FRED` from the bitmask, so it now includes only `X86_CR4_SMEP | X86_CR4_SMAP | X86_CR4_UMIP | X86_CR4_FSGSBASE | X86_CR4_CET`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, CR4 pinning will no longer treat the FRED bit as one of the immutable post-initialization CR4 bits. This means the kernel will not enforce or preserve FRED through the CR4 pinning mechanism, allowing it to be managed separately or avoiding incorrect pinning behavior on CPUs/configurations where FRED should not be part of that set.

Author: Kees Cook <kees@kernel.org>

    x86/cpu: Use pinning mask for CR4 bits needing to be 0
    
    The X86_CR4_FSGSBASE bit of CR4 should not change after boot[1]. Older
    kernels should enforce this bit to zero, and newer kernels need to
    enforce it depending on boot-time configuration (e.g. "nofsgsbase").
    To support a pinned bit being either 1 or 0, use an explicit mask in
    combination with
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the fix for the CR4 pinning logic. The key change is the explicit pinning mask: `cr4_pinned_mask = X86_CR4_SMEP | X86_CR4_SMAP | X86_CR4_UMIP | X86_CR4_FSGSBASE;`, but the corrected handling only applies those bits via the mask, e.g. `if (unlikely((val & cr4_pinned_mask) != cr4_pinned_bits))` and `val = (val & ~cr4_pinned_mask) | cr4_pinned_bits;`. In `cr4_init()`, the code also uses `cr4 = (cr4 & ~cr4_pinned_mask) | cr4_pinned_bits;`, preventing unintended forced enablement of a pinned bit outside the intended mask. Since the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the incorrect inclusion of `X86_CR4_FRED` in the pinning mask, and this snippet shows the corrected mask/logic rather than that bug, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
